item1_theIndex.whyNotAMigration: src/db/migrate.mjs wraps each file in BEGIN...COMMIT; a CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY inside that block aborts ('cannot run inside a transaction block') and the index would never exist. item2_thePlanProof.pagesTouchedDifference: 185 pages per 500-row page of output on Travis (692 vs 507), 329 on Bastrop (836 vs 507)
item2_thePlanProof.extrapolationToAPass: Travis is 762 pages per rail (380,917 cells / 500), so the old plan walks ~141,000 index pages in one pass -- the primary key is 160,554 pages / 1.25 GB, i.e. effectively the whole of it -- while the new index's slice for one rail is ~2,245 pages / 17.5 MB. 65 rails per county sweep: ~81 GB of index walked on the pkey against ~1.19 GB (the whole new index) once. This is arithmetic on measured index geometry, labelled as arithmetic.
item2_thePlanProof.latencyIsNotGradedHere: READ THE WALL CLOCK AS INVALID ON THIS CONTAINER. The before run found 504 of its 500 heap pages in shared_buffers (hit=504, 4.19ms) and the after run found 2 (read=505, 21.80ms): ~8us per cached page against ~42us per page read from the OS cache. The two runs did not have the same cache state, so the difference measures cache warmth, not the plan. shared_buffers here is 128MB against a 1.25GB primary key, and the laptop's OS page cache serves those reads for free -- the charge this change removes is Neon's per-page read, which no local container reproduces.
item2_thePlanProof.verdict: PASS on the plan for both counties; UNMEASURED on latency, with the reason and the counter-measurement stated.

deviationsAndMistakes: I REGISTERED THE WORKTREE LATE. The mission says 'Register it under the property seat before working'; I registered P:/tmp/p298-scheduler-read-shape in _catalog/seat_register.json after the build was finished, at 2026-09-17T01:17Z. No other lane was affected (the path is new and nothing else read it), but the ordering was wrong and is declared rather than back-dated.

The fake pg client in test/p298-index-step.test.mjs was not faithful: it accepted `SET lock_timeout = $1`, which PostgreSQL refuses with 42601. That is why the build verb's own build path had never executed until this session -- the first real run found the bug immediately. Fixed, and the fake now enforces the server's rule with a non-vacuity test. LESSON for the fleet: a mock that accepts statements the server rejects turns a broken verb into a green suite.
openThreadsForTheNextContext: The index is NOT built on the factory store. The seat runs: node scripts/heavy-scan-lease.mjs list (expect no live holder), then build --apply --expect-host against the factory store, then verify, then the cold six-county run.

The cold grading is the only thing that can turn falsifier 1 from PASS-on-plan into PASS-on-time. The six-county warm baseline was 33 minutes (2026-09-16 20:00Z); cold Travis was ~6 min/rail. A cold run should be timed with scripts/p298-rail-pass-timing.mjs per county before and after, or by the six-county sweep itself.
